$doc: Every `throw` and `Promise.reject(` in production src/, named and reasoned.
Enforced by scripts/guard-throws.mjs (`npm run guard:throws`), per
decisions/34-errors-as-values.md: a KNOWN failure mode belongs in the
signature as a Result<T, E>; `throw` is reserved for a violated invariant —
a state that cannot exist unless the code is wrong.
Each entry is { match, count, reason }. `match` is a substring of the throw's
own source line (text, not a line number, so it survives edits above it);
`count` is EXACT — the guard fails if the real count is higher or lower, so
removing a throw means removing its entry in the same diff.
`reason` must name the invariant. 'defensive' is not an invariant.
HISTORY. Seeded by card 91 with the full inventory as it stood: 15 sites in
9 files. Card 92 removed the four src/infra/chrome-storage/area.ts entries —
the only throws in the tree that carried an EXPECTED failure — leaving 11 in
8 files. Cards 93 (providers) and 94 (MCP) found nothing left to remove in
their stacks; 94 deleted src/infra/mcp/budget.ts's `Promise.reject`, taking
it to 10 in 8 files. Card 95 removed the last two non-invariants: the two
src/options/components/SettingsSection.svelte rethrows (an expected storage
failure, now an error alert in the section) and src/content/relay.ts's
rethrow (a page tool's own failure, now a returned Result).
WHAT IS LEFT, AND WHY IT IS FINAL (card 95's audit). Seven sites in five
files, and every one of them asserts a WIRING invariant that no user input,
no network, no storage state and no page can reach:
- four `app-services.ts` guards: initialised exactly once, and read only
after the composition root has run;
- two `main.ts` mount-point guards: this surface's own index.html;
- one port-contract assertion in the options page's MCP test-connection
form.
Each one is reachable only by editing the code wrongly, which is precisely
decision 34's bar for `throw`. Adding an entry here now means either a new
invariant of the same kind — with the invariant NAMED, not 'defensive' — or
a decision record saying why the rule changed.
Test code (*.test.ts, testing/) is out of scope — see the guard's header.

src/options/app-services.ts.reason: Invariant: src/options/main.ts calls initOptionsServices exactly once, before mount(). A second call means two service bundles exist in one surface — two stores, two debounce maps — which is a wiring bug with no correct recovery.

Invariant: the composition root has run before any component reads a service. Reachable only from a module imported outside main.ts's graph — a structural mistake, and far better reported than papered over with an undefined port.

src/sidepanel/app-services.ts.reason: Invariant: src/sidepanel/main.ts calls initSidePanelServices exactly once. Two chat stores in one panel each hold their own debounce map and index-write queue and stop serialising against each other — the interleaving card 55 fixed.

src/sidepanel/app-services.ts.match: "[webmcp] side panel services are not initialised
src/sidepanel/app-services.ts.reason: Invariant: the composition root has run before any component reads a service. Same structural-mistake case as the options twin.

src/options/main.ts.reason: Invariant: #app is in this surface's OWN index.html, so its absence is a packaging bug. Card 91 introduced this in place of a `document.getElementById("app")!`, which handed mount() a null target and failed further from the cause.

src/sidepanel/main.ts.reason: Invariant: #app is in this surface's OWN index.html — same packaging-bug case as the options twin, same card-91 replacement of a non-null assertion.

src/options/forms/mcpTestConnection.ts.match: "discoverAllServerTools returned no result for a single config"
src/options/forms/mcpTestConnection.ts.reason: Invariant: discoverAllServerTools returns exactly one entry per config passed in (src/domain/tools/gateway.ts). A single-element input coming back empty violates that port's contract; it is not a reachable outcome of testing a connection.
